editorial.headline: Chicken Wholesale Has a National Opening—and a Bali Stop
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale chicken and processed chicken meat is nationally open to PMA, but foreign investors cannot register it in Bali under the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor considering Bali, the answer is direct: this activity cannot be registered there for PMA today. That finding sits beside—not against—a nationally open position. At national level, the record marks the activity TERBUKA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. The point is therefore not that wholesale chicken trade is off-limits to foreign capital in Indonesia. It is that the national opening does not override the Bali registration outcome set out for this activity.

The activity itself is specific and commercial: wholesale trade in chicken meat and processed chicken meat, including preserved chicken meat. It concerns the wholesale movement of those products, keeping both processed and preserved chicken meat within the stated scope. That inclusion gives the classification a clear commercial perimeter: it is not limited to fresh chicken meat alone, but expressly encompasses the processed and preserved forms named in the record. The description is concise, yet it establishes a coherent wholesale activity rather than a loose collection of food-related business lines.

Businesses may register this activity at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, or Besar scale. That breadth is worth reading plainly: the record does not confine the activity to one size of enterprise. It makes the classification available across the four named scales, from Mikro through Besar, for businesses whose activity falls within the stated wholesale scope. The scale entry answers the basic registration-position question without adding conditions that the record does not provide.

In Bali, however, the result changes decisively for PMA. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk to every scope in the record. Bali’s stated rule permanently blocks PMA registration, island-wide, for all KBLI assessed at Low or Medium-Low risk. On 13 May 2026, this activity was therefore blocked by that Bali moratorium, with the status Blocked (risk class). Nationally, the record permits a 100% foreign stake, but a foreign investor cannot register this PMA activity in Bali today. The Bali limitation is a location-specific registration barrier, not a different national foreign-ownership ceiling.
